section_1.title: The Leap: From Geometry to Abstraction (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Brief review of physical vectors (arrows in 2D/3D). Introduce the idea that 'vectors' don't have to be arrows—they can be any objects (functions, polynomials, matrices) that obey specific structural rules.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 2D arrow vs. a 'vector' representing the pitch and rhythm of a bird's song.

section_2.title: The Foundation: The Two Core Operations (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: Explain that a space is 'vectorial' only if it supports two operations: Vector Addition and Scalar Multiplication. Use a split-screen animation showing geometric arrows on one side and algebraic polynomials on the other.
section_2.example: Adding two polynomials (x + 1) + (2x + 3) = 3x + 4, mirroring how we add arrows head-to-tail.

section_3.title: The Eight Axioms: The Rules of the Game (1:45-3:15)
section_3.content: A high-speed visual walkthrough of the 8 axioms (Closure, Associativity, Commutativity, Zero vector, Inverse, etc.). Use an 'ingredient list' graphic to show that as long as these 8 laws are satisfied, the set is a Vector Space.
section_3.example: A 'Robot Factory' analogy: If the robot's logic system follows these 8 laws, it can exist in the Vector Space, regardless of whether its 'limbs' are numbers or functions.

section_4.title: Non-Example: Detecting Broken Spaces (3:15-4:15)
section_4.content: Critical knowledge point: Show why a set that doesn't include the Zero vector or fails closure under addition cannot be a vector space. Use a visual 'gate' animation where invalid objects are rejected.
section_4.example: A set of arrows restricted to only the first quadrant—addition is fine, but scalar multiplication by a negative number 'escapes' the set, breaking the space.

section_5.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Wrap up by emphasizing that abstraction allows us to apply linear algebra tools (bases, dimensions, transformations) to complex fields like Data Science and Quantum Mechanics.
section_5.example: The 'Universal Toolkit' metaphor: One set of mathematical laws (Vector Spaces) applied to everything from Spotify’s music recommendation algorithms to a cat’s movement simulation.
